# Thingstudio

> Thingstudio is a node-and-wire visual editor for microcontrollers. You build a flow on a canvas; it compiles to MicroPython and runs on the board. To write flows without the editor, start with the page 'Writing flows with an AI assistant' (ai-authoring), then the node catalog, and check each flow with the thingstudio-compile command.

## Pages

- [Home](https://docs.thingstudio.net/): Thingstudio is a visual, low-code way to program microcontrollers.

## Background

- [Event-driven programming](https://docs.thingstudio.net/background/event-driven/): An event-driven program waits for things to happen, and runs a piece of code for each one.
- [Flows, nodes and messages](https://docs.thingstudio.net/background/flows-and-nodes/): A Thingstudio program is a **flow**: a set of **nodes** joined by **wires**.
- [Node-RED](https://docs.thingstudio.net/background/node-red/): Node-RED is a free tool for wiring together devices, web services and APIs.
- [MicroPython](https://docs.thingstudio.net/background/micropython/): MicroPython is a version of Python 3 made to run on microcontrollers.

## If you already know

- [Node-RED](https://docs.thingstudio.net/coming-from/node-red/): Most of what you know carries over.
- [MicroPython](https://docs.thingstudio.net/coming-from/micropython/): Thingstudio sits on top of the MicroPython you already have.
- [Arduino and C](https://docs.thingstudio.net/coming-from/arduino/): If you've written setup() and loop() in C or C++, Thingstudio will feel different in three ways.

## Getting started

- [1. Install Thingstudio](https://docs.thingstudio.net/getting-started/): From a new board to a blinking LED, in six steps:
- [2. Tour the editor](https://docs.thingstudio.net/editor-tour/): Start Thingstudio if it isn't running: see step 1.
- [3. Install MicroPython](https://docs.thingstudio.net/installing-micropython/): Thingstudio runs on top of MicroPython, so the board needs it first.
- [4. Connect your board](https://docs.thingstudio.net/connecting/): Connect the board over USB so the editor can talk to it.
- [5. Install the runtime](https://docs.thingstudio.net/installing-runtime/): The runtime is the part of Thingstudio that runs on the board: it receives your flows and runs them.
- [6. Blink an LED](https://docs.thingstudio.net/first-flow/): Your first flow: make an LED blink once a second, using three nodes.
- [Installation details](https://docs.thingstudio.net/installation-details/): How Thingstudio is packaged, where it puts its files, how to upgrade and remove it, and how to build it from source.

## Tutorials

- [Overview](https://docs.thingstudio.net/tutorials/): Getting started ends with a blinking LED.
- [Tutorial flows](https://docs.thingstudio.net/tutorial-flows/): If you'd rather not build the tutorial flows from scratch, or you get stuck, their finished flow files are in the tutorials folder, below.
- [Two more blinks](https://docs.thingstudio.net/tutorials/two-more-blinks/): If you've followed the steps in Getting started you'll now have a board with a blinking LED.
- [Web Blink](https://docs.thingstudio.net/tutorials/blink-from-your-network/): If you've worked through Two more blinks, you have a board whose LED blinks on a timer.
- [Blink from anywhere](https://docs.thingstudio.net/tutorials/blink-from-anywhere/): This tutorial is still being checked on a board.
- [A sensor display](https://docs.thingstudio.net/sensor-display/): This tutorial is being reworked.

- [Flow lifecycle](https://docs.thingstudio.net/flow-lifecycle/): How a flow is saved, opened, deployed and disconnected.
- [The Thingstudio folder](https://docs.thingstudio.net/thingstudio-folder/): Thingstudio keeps its own files in one folder on your computer:

## Boards and networks

- [Supported hardware](https://docs.thingstudio.net/supported-hardware/): The boards, processors, displays, touch panels, sensors and other hardware below have built-in support.
- [Boards and processors](https://docs.thingstudio.net/boards/): Each board and processor has a definition file that says which pins a flow may use.
- [Custom firmware for classic ESP32](https://docs.thingstudio.net/custom-firmware/): A MicroPython image with Thingstudio's runtime and every flow library built in, for classic ESP32 boards with 4 MB of flash and no PSRAM (ESP32-D0WD and simila…
- [Connecting over WiFi](https://docs.thingstudio.net/wifi-connection/): The editor can connect to a board over WiFi instead of USB.
- [WiFi provisioning](https://docs.thingstudio.net/wifi-provisioning/): You can leave a flow's WiFi network and password out, and enter them on the board when it first starts.

## Node reference

- [Overview](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/): Every built-in node has its own page, covering what it does, its properties and its output.

## General

- [inject](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/inject/): Sends one message with a fixed payload each time you click its ▶ icon while the editor is connected to the board.
- [startup](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/startup/): Sends one message with a fixed payload each time the flow starts.
- [timer](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/timer/): Sends a count that goes up by one at a fixed interval.
- [function](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/function/): Runs your own MicroPython on each message, for anything no other node does.
- [change](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/change/): Sets or deletes one value, on the message or in a flow variable, then passes the message on.
- [delay](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/delay/): Passes each message on unchanged, after a wait.
- [filter](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/filter/): Passes a message on only when it's worth sending, and drops the rest.
- [journal](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/journal/): Keeps the recent history of a number, as rows of average, minimum and maximum, the way RRDtool and Cacti do.
- [debug](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/debug/): Prints each message's payload to the console, to see what is flowing through a wire.

## Network

- [wifi status](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/wifi-status/): Reports the board's WiFi connection state.
- [wifi gate](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/wifi-gate/): Passes a message through unchanged while the board's WiFi is connected, and drops it while it isn't.
- [ntp](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ntp/): Sets the board's clock from the internet and sends the time, as text for a display or as Unix time.
- [udp receive](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/udp-receive/): Listens on a UDP port and emits one message per datagram received.
- [mqtt subscribe](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/mqtt-subscribe/): Sends a message for each message that arrives on an MQTT topic.
- [http request](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/http-request/): Makes one HTTP request per incoming message and returns the response.
- [http in](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/http-in/): Starts a web server on the board and sends a message for each request to a path.
- [http response](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/http-response/): Sends the reply to a request that arrived through an http in node.
- [udp send](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/udp-send/): Sends a message's payload as a UDP datagram to a fixed host and port.
- [mqtt publish](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/mqtt-publish/): Publishes each message's payload to an MQTT topic.

## Bluetooth

- [ble scan](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-scan/): Listens for Bluetooth LE advertisements, such as beacons and BLE sensors, and sends one message per advertisement.
- [ble advertise](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-advertise/): Advertises over Bluetooth LE: the board's name, and each message's payload as manufacturer or service data.
- [ble characteristic in](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-characteristic-in/): Sends a message each time a connected device writes a Bluetooth LE characteristic.
- [ble characteristic out](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-characteristic-out/): Sets a Bluetooth LE characteristic to each message's payload, for a connected device to read, and notifies the devices that subscribed.
- [ble uart in](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-uart-in/): Receives text from a connected device over Bluetooth LE, through the Nordic UART Service that terminal apps use.
- [ble uart out](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-uart-out/): Sends text to the devices connected over Bluetooth LE, through the Nordic UART Service.
- [ble read](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-read/): Reads a characteristic of another Bluetooth LE device for each message that arrives, and sends the value on.
- [ble write](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-write/): Writes each message's payload to a characteristic of another Bluetooth LE device.
- [ble notify](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-notify/): Subscribes to a characteristic of another Bluetooth LE device and sends a message each time it sends a new value.
- [BLE config](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble/): The board's Bluetooth name, shared by every ble node in a flow.
- [BLE peer](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ble-peer/): Another Bluetooth LE device the board connects to, such as a sensor or another board.

## Hardware

- [interrupt](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/interrupt/): Sends a message the moment a pin changes state.
- [eswitch](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/eswitch/): Reports when a switch opens or closes, ignoring contact bounce.
- [ebutton](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/ebutton/): Reports presses, releases, long presses and double clicks from one button, ignoring contact bounce.
- [adc](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/adc/): Reads an analog pin, and sends the reading when it moves past the set bounds, and at a fixed interval if one is set.
- [encoder](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/encoder/): Reads a rotary encoder (a quadrature knob) and sends its value each time it turns.
- [neopixel](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/neopixel/): Lights a WS2812 (NeoPixel) strip: sets its pixels from each message, then writes the strip.
- [gpio out](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/gpio-out/): Sets a pin high or low from each message.
- [pwm out](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/pwm-out/): Drives a PWM signal on a pin, for dimming an LED, setting a motor's speed, or any other variable duty cycle.
- [display spi](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/display-spi/): Pushes an already-rendered frame to an SPI color TFT panel.
- [display i2c](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/display-i2c/): Pushes an already-rendered frame to an I2C mono OLED panel.
- [bme280](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/bme280/): Reads a BME280 or BMP280 temperature, humidity and pressure sensor at a fixed interval.
- [touch](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/touch-i2c/): Raw touch input, for flows that don't use the GUI.
- [i2c device](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/i2c/): Talks to an I2C device that has no node of its own.
- [I2C bus](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/i2c-bus/): An I2C bus is shared by one or more devices.
- [Touch panels](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/touch-panel/): A touch panel is a capacitive touch screen on an I2C bus.
- [GUI](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes/gui/): The GUI nodes are provisional: their properties and the page layout may change between releases.

## Extending and automating

- [Node conventions](https://docs.thingstudio.net/node-conventions/): A node moves a message from one point in a flow to the next.
- [Writing custom nodes](https://docs.thingstudio.net/custom-nodes/): A custom node is two files sharing a base name: <name>.node.json (the descriptor) and <name>.node.py (the behavior), placed in the backend's ~/.thingstudio/cus…
- [Writing flows with an AI assistant](https://docs.thingstudio.net/ai-authoring/): This page is for an AI assistant (or a person) writing a Thingstudio flow file or a custom node in the user's folder, without the editor.
- [Check a flow without the editor](https://docs.thingstudio.net/check-a-flow/): thingstudio-compile compiles and checks a flow file from the command line, with the same errors the editor gives.
- [Command line](https://docs.thingstudio.net/command-line/): Options for starting Thingstudio, a way to install the runtime and run flows without the editor, and a check for a flow file.
- [Node catalog](https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes-catalog/): This is the flow-file reference.

## Troubleshooting

- [Debugging & troubleshooting](https://docs.thingstudio.net/debugging/): The **console** shows what the board and Thingstudio report: deploy results, node errors, and what debug nodes and print() send.
- [FAQ](https://docs.thingstudio.net/faq/): Ask questions, and show what you've built, in GitHub Discussions.
